::: {#sol-loss-at-start}

The [cross-entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-cross-entropy) loss of one image is $-\log$ of the probability the network gives its true class.
If every probability is $\frac{1}{10}$,
every image's loss is $-\log \frac{1}{10} = \log 10$,
and so is their mean.

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
start_loss = nn.functional.cross_entropy(mlp(x_test), y_test).item()
print(start_loss, np.log(10))
```

`nn.functional.cross_entropy` takes the [logits](#def-logits) and the true digits,
and returns the mean loss over the [test set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-test-set),
`r sprintf("%.3f", py$start_loss)`,
close to $\log 10 \approx `r sprintf("%.3f", log(10))`$.
A training run whose first loss is far from $\log C$,
for $C$ classes,
is worth checking for a bug before it runs further.

:::
